Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etaleChart_restrict_coordRingHom: The restricted chart is the composite of the inclusion of the smaller open subscheme with the chart. Pullback of functions therefore first takes the old chart’s pullback and then restricts to the smaller open. After identifying the section rings, this is the asserted composite on polynomial functions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_etaleChart_coord_add_smul: Replace only coordinate j₂ by its sum with t times coordinate j₁. The j₂ partial derivation gives one on the new section because it gives one on the old j₂ coordinate, kills coordinate j₁, and kills the scalar t. The differential matrix is the identity with column j₂ replaced, so its determinant is that same partial derivative, which is one. The unit determinant criterion gives an étale chart with these coordinates on the whole open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_etaleChart_coord_add_smul_chartPa: Take the chart obtained by the shear adding t times coordinate j₁ to coordinate j₂. In terms of the new coordinates, the old j₂ coordinate is the new j₂ coordinate minus t times the unchanged j₁ coordinate. Thus the new j₁ partial derivation evaluates to one on the old j₁ coordinate, to the negative of t on the old j₂ coordinate, and to zero on all others. The new partial derivations at the other indices have their usual dual values on all old coordinates. The chain rule expresses each new derivation from these values in the old partial basis, giving both asserted formulas.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_etaleChart_coord_eq_of_isUnit_jac: The old chart makes the section ring formally smooth over the base field. A unit determinant means the differentials of the proposed coordinates form a basis, so the differential criterion makes polynomial evaluation at those sections formally étale. The smooth ambient scheme gives a section ring of finite type over the field, and hence finitely presented over the Noetherian polynomial ring. Thus the evaluation map is étale. The associated morphism to affine space is the required chart and pulls back the variables to the given sections.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_etaleChart_restrict_coord_eq_of_j: Let g be the determinant of the proposed differentials in the old coordinate basis. Since g lies outside the prime of x, its affine basic open contains x. Its section ring is the localization at g, where the determinant becomes a unit. The coordinate basis of the old chart localizes to a basis there, and the restricted chart gives formal smoothness over the base field. The differential criterion followed by finite presentation makes evaluation at the restricted proposed sections étale. The chart from this evaluation has the required restricted coordinates.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_etaleChart_update_coord_of_partia: Replace the j₁-th section by the proposed section and retain all other coordinates. The differential matrix in the old coordinate basis is the identity with only column j₁ replaced. Its determinant is the j₁-th coefficient of the proposed differential, namely the indicated partial derivative. This element lies outside the prime of x. Apply the determinant criterion on its basic open to obtain a chart with the desired updated and restricted coordinates.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isUnit_mul_of_span_singleton_eq: Since the principal ideals coincide, write z = uy and y = bz for elements u and b of R. Substitution gives (bu − 1)y = 0. The nonzerodivisor condition on y gives bu = 1, so u is a unit and z is its product with y.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_unlabeled_index_partialDeriv_notM: Assume every old partial derivative of g in an unlabeled direction vanishes at x. Intersect the given chart with a chart witnessing strict normal crossing position for H and the listed divisors, taking an affine basic neighborhood of x in the intersection. There H is generated by one of the new coordinates, say y, since x lies in its support. The restriction of g is a unit times y because they generate the same principal ideal and y is a nonzerodivisor. Each labeled old coordinate likewise is a unit times the distinct new coordinate of its divisor. That new coordinate vanishes at x, and differentiation in the y direction kills it. The Leibniz rule therefore makes the derivative of each labeled old coordinate vanish at x in the y direction. Apply the chain rule to the restriction of g in that direction. Each labeled term vanishes by this calculation, and each unlabeled term vanishes by the assumption and compatibility with restriction. On the other hand, differentiating the unit times y in the y direction gives that unit modulo the prime of x. This contradiction yields an unlabeled index whose partial derivative lies outside the prime.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.formallySmooth_of_etaleChart: An affine étale chart makes the section ring formally étale over the polynomial ring. The chart respects the given scalar map, so its composition with the polynomial ring structure over the base field is the given structure on sections. The polynomial ring is formally smooth over the field, and composing with a formally étale map preserves formal smoothness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_chartPartialDeriv_restrict: Restriction takes the old chart’s coordinate sections to those of the restricted chart. The induced map on differentials therefore takes each coordinate differential to the corresponding one on the smaller open. Expanding df in the old differential basis and mapping the expansion shows that its coefficients restrict to the coefficients of the differential of the restricted f. These coefficients are the corresponding chart partial derivatives.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_mem_primeIdealOf_of_mem_of_le: The germ of a section at y is unchanged by restriction to a smaller neighborhood of y. A section belongs to the prime corresponding to y exactly when its germ lies in the maximal ideal of the stalk. The original section and its restriction therefore satisfy the same prime membership condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.notMem_support_of_restrictIdeal_eq_top_o: The support of the ideal sheaf pulled back to U is the inverse image of its original support. The restricted ideal is the unit ideal, whose support is empty. Consequently every point of U is outside the original support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.repr_sum_smul_apply: The expression is already the expansion in the given basis. Uniqueness of basis coordinates gives the specified coefficient at index i.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.D_mem_span_range_D_X: Induct on the polynomial. Constants have zero differential, and the differential of a sum is the sum of the differentials. When multiplying a polynomial by one variable, the product rule makes the differential a combination of the differential of the polynomial and the differential of that variable. This keeps it in the span of the variable differentials at every step.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordBasis_apply: The basis is constructed from the independent spanning family of coordinate differentials. Its vector at i is by construction the differential of the i-th coordinate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.formallyEtale_of_basis: Write P for the polynomial ring. The basis calculation makes the scalar-extension map on differentials an isomorphism. Its surjectivity gives formal unramifiedness over P. For formal smoothness, use the exact sequence for first cotangent homology of k → P → S. The connecting map from the first relative cotangent homology of S over P to the scalar-extended differentials has zero image, because its composite with the injective scalar-extension map is zero. Exactness therefore expresses every class in that relative homology as an image from the first cotangent homology over k. The latter vanishes by formal smoothness over k. Thus the relative homology vanishes, giving formal smoothness over P. Together the two properties give formal étaleness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.formallyEtale_of_isUnit_det: The unit determinant constructs a basis of coordinate differentials by the preceding results. The basis criterion for the formally smooth algebra S now gives formal étaleness over the coordinate polynomial ring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.formallyUnramified_of_mapBaseChange_surj: The transitivity sequence for differentials has the scalar-extension map followed by the projection to the relative differentials over the polynomial ring. Exactness makes this composite zero. Surjectivity of the first map therefore makes the projection zero, so the relative differential of every element of S vanishes. These differentials generate the relative module. It is thus zero, which is the formal unramifiedness criterion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inducedBasis_apply: The induced basis is built from the independent spanning family of images of the original basis vectors. Its i-th vector is the image of the i-th original basis vector.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inducedBasis_apply_D: The induced basis vector is the image of the original one. By hypothesis the original vector is the differential of the chosen element. Naturality sends that differential to the differential of the element's image in S′.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.linearIndependent_D_coord_of_isUnit_det: A square coefficient matrix over a commutative ring with unit determinant is invertible. The coordinate differentials whose coefficients form that matrix are therefore a basis, in particular a linearly independent family.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.linearIndependent_kaehlerMap_basis: For a formally étale map from S to S′, the differentials over k after extension of scalars identify with the differentials of S′ over k. Transport the scalar extension of the given basis under this isomorphism. Its vectors are the images of the original vectors, so they are linearly independent.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.linearIndependent_one_tmul_D_X: The differentials of the polynomial variables form a basis over the polynomial ring. Extending scalars to S gives a basis whose vectors are the tensors of 1 with those differentials. They are therefore linearly independent.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mapBaseChange_bijective_of_basis: On each vector of the scalar-extended polynomial differential basis, the map gives the corresponding coordinate differential. By hypothesis these are the vectors of a basis of the target module. A linear map taking one basis to the other at every index is an isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smul_one_tmul: In the tensor product, the scalar action on the left factor multiplies that factor. Acting by a on the tensor with left factor 1 therefore replaces 1 by a.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.span_range_D_X_eq_top: The differentials of all polynomials generate the module of Kähler differentials. Each lies in the span of the variable differentials by the preceding result. Hence that smaller family also generates the whole module.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.tensorKaehlerBasis_mapBaseChange: The i-th vector of the scalar-extended basis is the tensor of 1 with the i-th variable differential. The map on differentials sends that vector to the differential of the image of the variable in S, which is the i-th coordinate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.top_le_span_D_coord_of_isUnit_det: A unit determinant makes the coefficient matrix of the coordinate differentials invertible. Its columns then generate all coefficient vectors in the fixed basis, so the coordinate differentials span the whole module.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.top_le_span_kaehlerMap_basis: The relative differentials of S′ over S vanish by formal unramifiedness. Exactness of the transitivity sequence then makes the scalar-extension map onto the differentials of S′ over k surjective. The tensors of 1 with the original basis vectors span its source, and their images are the stated family. That family therefore spans the target.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.top_le_span_one_tmul_D_X: The variable differentials generate the module over the polynomial ring. Apply the scalar-extension spanning result to this generating family.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.top_le_span_range_one_tmul: Write any element of M as a finite linear combination of the given generators. Bilinearity expresses a pure tensor with that element as a sum of tensors with those generators, moving the coefficients from the base ring to the left factor by the balancing relation. Each such tensor is an A-multiple of the tensor with left factor 1. Since pure tensors generate the tensor product additively, the indicated tensors span over A.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_away_ideal_eq_span_and_formallyEt: Choose the principal localization and replacement coordinates from the construction with unit determinant. The coordinates taken from I generate its extension there, while the other coordinates come from the original family. The determinant criterion on that localization makes the map obtained by evaluating the polynomial variables at the replacement coordinates formally étale.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_away_ideal_eq_span_and_isUnit_det: Put A = S localized at q and let J be the extension of I to A. Choose finite generators for I. The residue differentials of their images span the residue differentials of all elements of J by the Leibniz rule, since J lies in the maximal ideal of A. Choose a basis of this span from those images and take the corresponding generators in I. The local generation criterion gives that these elements generate J. Complete their residue differentials to a basis by retaining a subset of the old coordinate differentials. The number of omitted old coordinates equals the number of chosen generators. Replace the omitted coordinates by these generators, using a bijection between their index sets. The resulting determinant is nonzero in the residue field of A, so its original value in S lies outside q. The ideal generated by the new coordinates from I and the ideal I have the same extension to A. By finite generation, clear the denominators in the local equalities to obtain an element g₁ outside q on whose principal localization the ideals agree. Localize at the product of g₁ and the determinant. This product lies outside q by primality, the ideal equality persists, and the determinant becomes a unit. The remaining coordinates were retained from the original family.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.formallyEtale_away_of_isUnit_det: For the original polynomial coordinates, the map to the localization is formally étale by composition with localization. Thus the localized algebra is formally smooth over k and its differentials have the basis obtained from the original coordinates. The determinant for the images of the new coordinates is the image of their determinant over S, since differentials and the coordinate basis are compatible with this localization. It is a unit by assumption, so the new differentials form a basis. The differential criterion for formal étaleness now applies to evaluation of the polynomial variables at the new coordinates.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_eq_span_of_tmul_D_mem_span: Let L be the ideal generated by the chosen family in J. Given y in J, express its residue differential as a combination of the chosen residue differentials, and lift the coefficients to A. Subtract that combination of the chosen elements from y. Its residue differential is zero by the Leibniz rule, since the chosen elements lie in the maximal ideal. The vanishing criterion puts this difference in mJ, where m is the maximal ideal. Thus J = L + mJ. The quotient J/L is finite, so Nakayama’s lemma gives J/L = 0.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_eq_of_map_eq_of_away_mul: In the localization at the product g₁d, the product is a unit and hence g₁ is a unit. The map from S therefore factors through the localization at g₁. Extending the equality of the two ideals along this factorization gives equality in the localization at g₁d.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_maximalIdeal_mul_of_tmul_D_eq_zero: Write m for the maximal ideal. The surjection A/mJ → A/J has square-zero kernel J/mJ because J is contained in m. Formal smoothness of A/J supplies a k-algebra section. Subtract the composite through this section from the quotient map A → A/mJ. The difference takes values in J/mJ and is a k-derivation because the product of any two values is zero. By the universal property of differentials it gives an A-linear map from Ω(A/k) to J/mJ. If the residue differential of z is zero then all coordinates of dz in the given basis lie in m. Since m annihilates J/mJ, the linear map sends dz to zero. For z in J that value is the class of z in J/mJ, so z belongs to mJ.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.repr_mem_maximalIdeal_of_tmul_eq_zero: Extend the given basis of M to the residue field. In the resulting basis the coordinates of 1 ⊗ x are exactly the residues of the original coordinates of x, by the balancing relation. If 1 ⊗ x is zero then every reduced coordinate is zero, so all coordinates of x lie in the maximal ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.residue_det_ne_zero_of_tmul_eq_basis: Reduce the original basis to obtain a basis of the residue tensor product. The column of the reduced vector 1 ⊗ G(j) in that basis is the reduction of the column of G(j) in the original basis. The determinant of this reduced matrix is therefore the residue of the original determinant. Its columns form the given new basis, so the matrix is invertible and its determinant is nonzero.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dTensor_apply: The map on the kernel of the residue homomorphism is the restriction of the universal derivation followed by extension to the residue field. Its value at x is consequently 1 ⊗ dx.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_local_parameters: Write m for the maximal ideal and κ for the residue field. Noetherianity makes m finitely generated, so κ ⊗ m is finite-dimensional. Choose a basis and lift each basis vector to an element of m using the surjectivity of x ↦ 1 ⊗ x. Nakayama’s lemma shows that the lifts generate m because their residues span m/m². Their residue differentials are independent by injectivity of the conormal differential.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_local_parameters_and_dual_derivat: Choose generators of the maximal ideal whose differentials are independent after reduction to the residue field. On the span of these reduced differentials take the dual coordinate functionals, and extend each to the whole reduced differential space. Choose an A-basis of the differential module. Lift the values of each functional on the reduced basis to A and extend those values A-linearly. Let M be the matrix of evaluations of the lifted functionals on the parameter differentials. It reduces to the identity, so its determinant is a unit in the local ring. Take the linear combinations of the lifted functionals given by the rows of M⁻¹. They evaluate on the parameter differentials as the identity matrix. Composing them with the universal derivation gives the required derivations.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.injective_liftBaseChange_dTensor: Write an element in the kernel as 1 ⊗ x with x in the kernel I of the residue map, using surjectivity of the map from I to its residue tensor product. Its image is 1 ⊗ dx, so the vanishing criterion for the conormal differential gives x in I². Every product of two elements of I dies in the tensor product because the first factor acts by zero on the residue field. Thus 1 ⊗ x is zero, proving injectivity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.linearIndependent_tensor_D_of_ideal_eq_k: Identify I with the kernel of the residue map using the given equality of ideals. This identification carries each input tensor to the tensor of the same element of A and preserves its differential. The independence result for the kernel therefore applies to this family.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.linearIndependent_tensor_D_of_ker: The residue-field linear map from the tensor product of the kernel ideal to the tensor product of the differential module is injective. It takes each given tensor to the tensor of the corresponding differential. Applying injectivity to any finite linear relation among the images reduces it to a relation among the given independent tensors, so its coefficients vanish.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.linearIndependent_tensor_D_of_maximalIde: The residue field is the quotient by the maximal ideal, so the kernel of the residue map is precisely that ideal. Apply the independence result for an ideal equal to the kernel.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_ker_sq_of_tmul_D_eq_zero: Let κ be the residue field and I the kernel of A → κ. The conormal differential sends the class of x in I/I² to 1 ⊗ dx in κ ⊗ Ω(A/k). Since A is formally smooth over k, the kernel of this differential computes the first cotangent homology of κ over k. This homology vanishes because κ is formally smooth over k as well. Thus a zero differential forces the class of x in I/I² to vanish, which means x lies in I².
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.one_tmul_residueField_surjective: Let κ be the residue field of A. In a pure tensor c ⊗ x with c in κ, lift c to an element a of A. The balancing relation gives c ⊗ x = 1 ⊗ ax. Every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors, and additivity combines these to give a single tensor of the form 1 ⊗ y.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.tmul_eq_zero_of_toCotangent_eq_zero: The zero class in I/I² means that x lies in I². Write x as a finite sum of products ab with a and b in I. In the tensor product with I, the term 1 ⊗ ab equals ā ⊗ b by balancing. Since I lies in the maximal ideal, every such ā is zero in the residue field. The sum is therefore zero.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_subschemeMap_isOpenImmersion: The closed subscheme defined by the pulled-back ideal on V is the fibre product of V and the closed subscheme defined by D over W. Take its projection to the latter closed subscheme. That projection is the base change of the open immersion V → W, so it is an open immersion. The fibre product square gives the required equality of composites.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOpenImmersion_subschemeMap: The fibre product construction supplies an open immersion with the required composite into W. Any other map with the same composite agrees with it because the closed immersion into W is a monomorphism. The given map is therefore an open immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_comap: Restricting to an open subscheme preserves the local description by one non-zero-divisor. The pulled-back closed subscheme maps to the original divisor by an open immersion, which is smooth. Composing it with the original divisor's smooth map to the base field gives the smooth structure map of the pulled-back divisor.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.algebraMap_X_inl: The joint evaluation sends an old variable to the corresponding coordinate in S, viewed as a constant polynomial in the new variables.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.algebraMap_X_inr: The joint evaluation sends a new variable to the variable with the same index in the polynomial ring over S.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.algebraMap_eq_mvPolynomial_map: The indicated algebra structure is defined by applying the coefficient map to each polynomial coefficient and leaving the variables in place. Its structure map is thus the specified polynomial map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.algebraMap_eq_sumEval: The target algebra over the combined polynomial ring is defined by the joint evaluation. Its algebra map is that evaluation on every polynomial.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.algebraMap_eq_sumEvalIter: The iterated polynomial ring is given its algebra structure by the map splitting off the first block as coefficients. The structure map therefore evaluates by this splitting.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.bijective_sumEvalIter: The map from iterated to combined polynomials is a left inverse, proving injectivity. It is also a right inverse, so it gives a preimage of every iterated polynomial and proves surjectivity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coord_inl: A coordinate is the image of its polynomial variable. For a first-block index, the variable formula identifies that image with the corresponding old coordinate embedded as a constant polynomial.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coord_inr: By definition the coordinate is the image of the variable at that index. The second-block variable formula identifies that image with the corresponding new variable.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.formallyEtale_mvPolynomial_map: Adjoining the same variables to R and A is base change along the map from R to its polynomial ring. The base change ring identifies with the polynomial ring over A, with each old polynomial mapping by applying R → A to its coefficients. Since formal étaleness is preserved under base change and isomorphism, that coefficient map is formally étale.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.formallyEtale_mvPolynomial_sum: Factor the joint evaluation through the iterated polynomial ring. The first map is formally étale because it is the isomorphism separating the two variable blocks. The second applies the formally étale coefficient map after adjoining the new variables, so it is formally étale by base change. Compatibility of the algebra maps identifies the composite with the joint evaluation, which is then formally étale.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.formallyEtale_sumEvalIter: The algebra map for the iterated polynomial ring is bijective by the two inverse formulas. It is therefore an algebra isomorphism over the combined polynomial ring. An isomorphism is formally étale.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.formallyEtale_trans: The combined polynomial ring maps formally étale to the polynomial ring over S in the new variables by the preceding result. The map from that ring to T is formally étale by assumption. Their composite is the given structure map to T by the scalar tower condition and is formally étale.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iterToSumHom_C_C: The map first interprets a coefficient of the outer polynomial as a polynomial in the first block. An original scalar a is constant in both blocks, so it maps to the scalar a in the combined polynomial ring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iterToSumHom_C_X: An inner variable viewed as a constant outer polynomial is evaluated at the variable with the same index in the first block of the combined ring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iterToSumHom_X: The evaluation sends each outer variable to the corresponding variable in the second block of the combined ring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iterToSumHom_sumEvalIter: The composite fixes the scalars by the constant formulas. A first-block variable becomes an inner coefficient variable and then returns to its first-block position. A second-block variable becomes an outer variable and then returns to its second-block position. The two maps preserve the ring operations, so induction on polynomial expressions shows that the composite fixes every polynomial.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mapCoeffAlgebra_isScalarTower: Compare the direct evaluation with the map through the iterated polynomial ring on scalars and both blocks of variables. On scalars the maps agree by compatibility of the coefficient maps. For the first block both give the image in S of the old variable as a constant polynomial. For the second block both give the same outer variable. These generators determine the ring maps, so the composite and direct maps agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mapCoeffAlgebra_isScalarTower_of_isScala: Along the composite, a scalar first becomes a constant with coefficient in the old polynomial ring and then maps coefficientwise into S. The original scalar tower identifies this coefficient with the direct image of the scalar in S. The resulting constant polynomial agrees with the direct map into the target, establishing the tower.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sumEvalAlgebra_isScalarTower: Evaluation is a homomorphism of k-algebras. Hence the direct scalar map from k to the target agrees with the composite through the polynomial source. This compatibility gives the scalar tower.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sumEvalIter_C: The evaluation preserves the scalar map from k. In the iterated polynomial ring a scalar is embedded as a constant in the inner ring and then as a constant in the outer ring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sumEvalIter_X_inl: The evaluation substitutes the inner variable with index i for the first-block variable, viewing that inner variable as an outer constant.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sumEvalIter_X_inr: The evaluation substitutes the outer variable with index j for the second-block variable.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sumEvalIter_iterToSumHom: The composite fixes every outer constant by the preceding result. Each outer variable is sent to its second-block variable and then back to the original outer variable. These constants and variables generate the outer ring, so the composite fixes every polynomial.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sumEvalIter_iterToSumHom_C: For an outer constant with inner coefficient r, check the composite on the generators of the inner polynomial ring. A scalar returns as the same scalar in both rings. An inner variable becomes a first-block variable and then returns as an inner variable embedded as an outer constant. Additivity and multiplicativity extend this identity to every r.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceGlobalSectionsHom_C: Apply the evaluation description to a constant polynomial. Its value is the coefficient mapped from k to the global sections of the base spectrum and then pulled back to affine space.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceGlobalSectionsHom_X: Apply the evaluation description of the map on global sections to the indexed variable. Its value is the coordinate section with that index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceGlobalSectionsHom_eq_eval₂Hom: Under the affine-space identification with the spectrum of the polynomial ring, the map on global sections pulls a variable back to its coordinate function. On constants it is pullback along the structure map to the spectrum of k. These values uniquely specify polynomial evaluation at the coordinate functions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.algebraMap_quotient_apply: The structure map from k to R/I is the structure map to R followed by the quotient map. It therefore sends a scalar to the class of its image in R.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.algebraMap_quotient_map_mk: The image ideal in A contains the images of all elements of I. Thus the map from R to A induces a map on the stated quotients. By its construction the class of r goes to the class of its image in A.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appLE_top_comp_app: Naturality of the pullback on sections says that restriction from X to U commutes with pulling back along f and restricting to the inverse image of U. Compose this square with the pullback of global sections along p. The composite pullback is the one along the structural morphism of W, giving the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.app_sectionsAlgebraMap: Apply the naturality equality for the two composites to the global section of the spectrum of k represented by a. The scalar structure maps are precisely those composites, so the resulting equality is the desired compatibility.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etale_homOfVector_of_ringHom_etale: Form the map from U to affine space using the given tuple of sections. Identify the global sections of affine space with the polynomial ring and those of the open subscheme U with the original sections over U. Under these identifications its map on global sections agrees with f on variables by construction. It agrees on constants because the map to affine space is over the spectrum of k and f respects the prescribed scalar map. Since constants and variables generate the polynomial ring, the two maps agree. Both schemes are affine, so the étaleness of f implies étaleness of the scheme map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_chart_ideal_eq_span_coord: Start with an affine étale chart around x and write R for its section ring and I for the center ideal. The prime q of x contains I because x is in the support. The center over this open is affine with section ring R/I, since its closed immersion induces a surjection with kernel I. This quotient is formally smooth over k by smoothness of the center. Localization at q preserves formal smoothness of the quotient by the extended ideal. Apply the local normal form to obtain a principal localization at an element outside q and a new tuple for which polynomial evaluation is formally étale. The selected entries of the tuple generate the localized center ideal. The localization is the section ring of a basic open containing x. Transport the evaluation map to this section ring. The ring is of finite type over k and hence of finite type over the polynomial ring under evaluation. The polynomial ring is Noetherian, so evaluation is of finite presentation, making it étale. The chart defined by this étale evaluation has the new tuple as coordinates. On the basic open the center ideal is the extension of I, which is therefore generated by the selected coordinates.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_chart_restrictIdeal_eq_coordIdeal: Take the affine chart where the section ideal of the center is generated by a subset of the coordinates. On this affine open the equality of section ideals identifies the restricted ideal sheaf with the pullback of the corresponding coordinate-subspace ideal. The open contains x and gives the claimed chart.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_etaleChart_coord_eq: The map to affine space associated to the given tuple is étale by the affine criterion for the given ring map. This makes it an étale chart. Pullback of each coordinate recovers the corresponding entry of the tuple, and the identification of global sections of the open subscheme with sections on U gives the desired equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.formallySmooth_quotient_map_of_isLocaliz: Extending I to the localization and then taking the quotient gives the localization of R/I at the image of the original multiplicative set. Localization is formally étale and hence formally smooth. Its structure map from k agrees with the composite through R/I, so composition with the assumed formally smooth map from k to R/I gives the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_nil_of_smoo: At each point of the center choose an étale chart in which its ideal is a coordinate ideal, using smoothness of the ambient scheme and the center. For the empty divisor list there are no divisor coordinates or compatibility conditions. The coordinate description of the center is the remaining condition and holds on the chosen chart.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_le_primeIdealOf: On U, the support of Z is the common zero locus of its section ideal. An element outside the prime of x would give a basic open containing x. If that element were in the ideal of Z, this would contradict membership in its common zero locus. Every element of the ideal therefore lies in the prime.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_algebraMap_eq_map_map_of_algEquiv: The R-algebra isomorphism from L to M carries the image of each element of R in L to its image in M. The composite through L therefore gives the same map from R to M, and extension of ideals along this composite is successive extension.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_basicOpen_of_notMem_primeIdealOf: Under the affine identification of U with the spectrum of its section ring, x corresponds to the stated prime. A prime lies in the principal open of g exactly when it avoids g. The affine identification carries that principal open to the basic open of g in X, so x belongs to it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofIdealTop_ideal_top: The ideal sheaf attached to J assigns to an affine open the extension of J along restriction to that open. At the whole affine scheme that restriction is the identity, so its ideal is J.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_eq_coordIdeal_of_ideal_eq_: The open subscheme U is affine, so it suffices to compare the ideals on its global section ring. Transporting the section ideal of Z to that ring carries its generators to the pullbacks of the specified coordinate sections, by the definition of chart coordinates. The coordinate-subspace ideal is generated by those coordinate sections in affine space. Pullback along the chart extends that ideal to the span of their pullbacks. Thus both sheaves have the same global ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sectionsAlgebraMap_apply_eq: The scalar action on sections over U is defined by first viewing the scalar as a global section of the spectrum of k, then pulling it back to X and restricting to U. The displayed map is this same composite evaluated on the scalar.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ι_appLE_eq_topIso_inv: The map from sections on U to global sections of the open subscheme U is induced by restricting to the image of that whole subscheme. The image is U itself, so the restriction on X is the identity. The resulting map is the canonical identification in the direction from sections on U to its global sections.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasSmoothCoordCodim_iff: Unfold the coordinate condition of codimension c. At every point it requires an open neighbourhood of the image and a smooth map from that open to affine c-space over the field. The kernel ideal there is the pullback of the ideal generated by all c coordinates. These are exactly the data on the right.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_iso_hom:
Use the original chart at the point of X, then transport its neighbourhood to X″ using the inverse isomorphism. The coordinate map on the transported open is the restriction of the inverse isomorphism followed by the old smooth coordinate map. It is smooth and compatible with the new structure map because the isomorphism is over the field.

The kernel of the transported closed immersion pulls back from the original kernel along that inverse isomorphism. Restriction to the transported open therefore pulls back the coordinate description from the original open. Functoriality of pullback identifies it with the origin ideal pulled back along the transported coordinate map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iso_hom_comp: For a point of X₀ use the original chart at its image in X. The composite immersion has the same image point in the target, and precomposing with a source isomorphism gives the same kernel ideal. The original chart and its kernel description therefore provide the required witnesses.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_comp_iso: Identify Z with Y by the inverse of the isomorphism. Under this identification the composite closed immersion is the base change of f. Its kernel is therefore the pullback of the original kernel along the inverse isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_eq_comap_of_isPullback: A closed immersion is given by its kernel ideal. Base change takes that ideal to its pullback, as one sees on affines by taking the quotient by the extended ideal. The given pullback square identifies the resulting closed immersion with the map in the statement.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_resLE: The restriction to U forms a pullback square with the open inclusion. Apply the kernel formula for base change of a closed immersion along that inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.resLE_comp_ι: The restriction square commutes. The composite through the restricted map to U and its inclusion is therefore the inclusion of the inverse-image open followed by f.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.resLE_open:
At a point of the source over O, apply the original condition to its image point in the original source. It gives an open U and a smooth coordinate map on U. Use the inverse image of U in O as the new neighbourhood. Its coordinate map is the restricted inclusion into U followed by the original coordinate map, so it is smooth. The restriction square gives the required equality of maps to the spectrum of k.

The kernel of the restricted immersion is the pullback of the original kernel to O. Restricting it to the new neighbourhood is the same as pulling back the original kernel restricted to U. Substitute the coordinate description on U and compose the two pullbacks. This gives the pullback of the origin ideal along the new coordinate map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_resLE: The restricted map to U is the base change of f along the open inclusion of U in Y. Smoothness is preserved by base change.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_etaleChart_restrictIdeal_eq_coord: Apply the smooth-center chart theorem to write the divisor ideal as a coordinate ideal indexed by S. The Cartier property also gives a neighborhood of x with an equation f that is a nonzerodivisor. Choose a common basic open containing x, principal in both neighborhoods. On it the restricted chart coordinates indexed by S generate the same ideal as the restriction of f. If S were empty, f would become zero there. Then some power of the element defining this basic open would annihilate f, so that power would be zero by the nonzerodivisor property. Inverting it would give the zero ring, impossible on an open containing x. If S contained two distinct indices, the two chart coordinates would belong to the same principal ideal on the common open. The chart remains formally étale after localization, so the dual partial derivations force this ideal to contain one. The ideal is contained in the prime of x because x lies in the divisor support, which rules this out. Thus S consists of one index and the original chart has the required single coordinate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_ideal_eq_span_singleton_of_opens_: The equality of the underlying opens identifies the affine opens and their section rings. The generator on the second open therefore generates the ideal on the first open as well.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_eq_bot_of_opens_eq: Two affine opens with the same underlying open are equal as affine opens. Under this equality their section rings and ideal values agree, so the vanishing transfers.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_singleton: The only member of the list is smooth by hypothesis. A point on the divisor has an étale chart where the divisor ideal is generated by one coordinate, and that coordinate gives the required assignment. At a point outside the divisor choose an étale chart inside the open complement of its support. The restricted ideal has empty support and hence is the unit ideal, which gives the assignment with no coordinate. In both cases the conditions concerning distinct list entries are vacuous.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.one_mem_of_coord_mem_span_singleton_of_n: Each of the two coordinates is a multiple of the generator h. Formal étaleness provides the two partial derivations that take value one on their own coordinate and zero on the other. Apply the quotient argument for two multiples of a common generator to conclude that the ideal contains one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.one_mem_of_mul_mem_of_dual_derivations: Work in the quotient by I, where f vanishes. The Leibniz rule then gives the residue of δ(cf) as the product of the residues of c and δ(f). For y₁ and y₂ the diagonal products with the indicated derivations equal one, while the two off-diagonal products equal zero. The product of the diagonal terms equals the product of the off-diagonal terms by commutativity. Thus one equals zero in the quotient and belongs to I.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_affineOpen_etale_over_affineSpace:
First restrict h to the intersection of V₀ with the inverse image of W₀, mapping that intersection to W₀. The point y belongs to the intersection and the restricted map remains smooth. Choose affine neighbourhoods of the point and its image on which the map on section rings is standard smooth. Viewed inside Y and X through the open inclusions, these are affine opens V and W with V contained in V₀, W contained in W₀, and h(V) contained in W.

The maps on sections agree under these open identifications, so the map for V and W is also standard smooth. Apply the affine factorization to obtain the étale map to a relative affine space over W. Its composite with the projection is the restriction of h, and the source open contains y.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_etale_mvPolynomial_ulift: Reindex the polynomial variables by the canonical bijection from the lifted index set to the original index set. This gives a polynomial-ring isomorphism that fixes the constants. Precomposing g with it preserves the original map on R and preserves étaleness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_etale_over_affineSpace_of_isStand: Standard smoothness factors the ring map through an étale map from a polynomial ring over R. Reindex its variables to the index set used for affine space. Taking spectra gives an étale morphism from the spectrum of S to the spectrum of that polynomial ring, which is the relative affine space over the spectrum of R. The equality of the composite on constants becomes the required equality of maps to the base.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_etale_over_affineSpace_resLE_of_i: Apply the affine factorization for standard smooth ring maps to the map on sections from W to V. Transport its étale map along the affine identifications of V and W with spectra, using the induced identification of relative affine spaces over the base. Isomorphisms preserve étaleness. Naturality of the affine-space projection identifies the composite to W with the restricted map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isAffineOpen_etale_resLE_le: Apply the preceding construction to the specified neighbourhoods of y and its image. It supplies the two contained affine opens, the relative affine space, and the étale factorization of the restricted map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.resLE_eq_isoSpec_conj_SpecMap_appLE: The canonical affine identifications turn the map of section rings into a map between the two affine opens, in the opposite direction. Its composite with the inclusion of W in X agrees with the composite of the inclusion of V with h by naturality of these identifications. The restricted scheme map has this same composite. Cancel the monomorphism given by the inclusion of W.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_resLE: Check smoothness on affine opens in the restricted source and target. Their images under the open inclusions into Y and X are affine, and the restricted map on their sections is the section-ring map of h on these images. Since h is smooth, each of these ring maps is smooth, proving the claim.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appLE_eq_appLE_comp_presheaf_map: Both sides first pull back from U to its full inverse image. On the right the subsequent restriction to A passes through B. Functoriality of restriction makes that composite the restriction directly to A.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_app_apply: Pullback of sections along a composite is the successive pullback, first along g from U and then along f from the inverse image of U under g. Evaluating on x gives the formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_presheaf_map_comp_map: Functoriality identifies the composite of the first two presheaf maps with the map of the composite arrow. Between fixed opens there is at most one inclusion arrow, so the composite arrow equals the third arrow. Precomposing with h preserves the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etaleChart_numCoords_add_one_of_hypersur: Restrict the ambient chart to the coordinate hypersurface H, omitting the coordinate indexed by j₁. The resulting chart has n − 1 coordinates. Choose a common affine neighborhood of y on H inside its domain and the domain of the second chart. Both chart restrictions have the same number of coordinates by the rank comparison for étale charts. Since j₁ is an index of the ambient chart, n is positive, so m′ + 1 = n.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etaleChart_numCoords_eq: Each chart gives a basis of the same module of Kähler differentials over k on the affine open. The section ring is nonzero because it maps to the nonzero stalk at x. Over this ring the finite rank is the number of basis vectors. Both chart dimensions therefore equal the same rank.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_ker_cons_of: At a point of the composite center, take the local coordinates provided by the hypothesis and denote the H-index by j₀. If an old divisor carried that same index, its ideal would coincide with the ideal of H on the chart. Compare with a chart for the strict normal crossing position of H and the old divisors on a common affine neighborhood of the point. The ideal of H is proper there because it lies in the ideal of the composite center. Both equal ideals must therefore have coordinate labels in the comparison chart. Those labels are distinct by injectivity, but equality of their principal ideals would force the ideal to be the unit ideal by cancellation for distinct chart coordinates. This contradiction shows that j₀ is unused by the old labels. Add it as the label of H and keep all the tail labels. The ideal of the composite center is generated by the lifted coordinates defining Z together with the H-coordinate, by taking the inverse image along the quotient by H. This is a coordinate ideal in the given chart, and the combined divisor labeling is injective.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_eq_top_of_restrictIdeal_eq_top: The canonical section-ring isomorphism from sections on V to global sections of its open subscheme carries the ideal on V to the global ideal of the restricted sheaf. This image contains one by hypothesis. Pulling one back along the isomorphism shows that the original ideal contains one, hence is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_ne_top_of_mem_support: A point of the support in V has a preimage in the corresponding open of the closed subscheme. Its section ring maps to the nonzero stalk at that preimage and is therefore nonzero. The section ideal is the kernel of the map to this ring. Since one maps to one, the kernel is proper.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_appLE_congr: Identify the two target opens using their equality. The maps then pull back to the same open and have the same source ring and target ring, so their kernels agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_comp_subschemeι_ideal_eq_comap: The inverse image of U under the composite closed immersion is obtained by taking the two inverse images in succession. The pullback on sections is the composite of the two pullback maps. On the affine inverse image in H, the ideal of Z is the kernel of the second map. The kernel of the composite is therefore its inverse image under the first pullback map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_comp_subschemeι_ideal_eq_span_coord: The composite kernel is the inverse image of the section ideal of Z under restriction to H. Write J for the ideal generated by the original coordinates indexed by S. The given description of Z says its ideal is the image of J. Restriction to H is surjective with kernel generated by the coordinate at j₀. The inverse image of the image of J is J plus that kernel, and this sum is generated by the coordinates indexed by S together with j₀.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_ideal_eq_ker_appLE: On the given affine open, the kernel ideal sheaf is defined by the kernel of pullback to the inverse image. The map of sections with that whole inverse image as its target is exactly the pullback map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_ker_comp_subschemeι: For each affine open in P, an element of the ideal of H pulls back to zero on H. Its further pullback to Z is also zero. This proves the inclusion in the kernel ideal on every affine open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_map_of_mul_mem_of_etale: Pass to the quotient of A by the extended ideal. It is étale, hence flat, over the source quotient because it arises by base change of the given étale map. Multiplication by the class of w on the source quotient is injective by hypothesis. Flatness preserves that injectivity after tensoring with the target quotient. The product assumption therefore forces the class of x to be zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_span_X_of_mul_X_mem: Set the j-th variable equal to zero while fixing the other variables and the coefficients. The image of the stated product is zero because it belongs to the ideal of the j-th variable. The image of the s-th variable is unchanged and nonzero. The polynomial ring is a domain, so the image of r is zero. This substitution acts as the identity modulo the ideal of the j-th variable, which gives membership of r in that ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofIdealTop_ideal_top: The sheaf defined by a global ideal assigns to an affine open the extension of that ideal along restriction. At the whole affine scheme this restriction is the identity and the ideal stays J.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.quotient_span_X_mul_X_cancel: Lift the two classes to polynomials and subtract. The s-th variable times the difference of the lifts lies in the ideal of the j-th variable. The cancellation criterion for distinct variables puts the difference itself in that ideal, so the classes are equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_eq_coordIdeal_of_isAffineO: On each affine open of the open subscheme U, the restricted ideal is generated by the images of the given chart coordinates. The ideal of the coordinate subspace in affine space is generated by its corresponding global coordinate sections. Pulling it back to the same affine open gives the identical generators, because the chart coordinates are those pullbacks viewed as sections on U. The ideals therefore agree on all affine opens.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_eq_coordIdeal_restrict: Pull back the equality on U along the inclusion of the smaller open subscheme. On one side this restricts I to V. On the other side it composes the coordinate-subspace pullback with the inclusion, giving the coordinate ideal of the restricted chart.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_eq_top_of_le_of_eq_top: Restriction to V factors through restriction to U. Pullback of the unit ideal along the inclusion of V is the unit ideal, giving the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.span_coord_eq_top_of_mem_span: In the polynomial quotient by the j-th variable, multiplication by the distinct s-th variable is injective. The affine chart map is étale, so this injectivity holds on the section-ring quotient by the j-th chart coordinate as well. The hypothesis says the image of the s-th coordinate sends one to zero in this quotient. Injectivity forces one to vanish there, so the defining principal ideal is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subschemeι_app_apply_eq_zero: For the closed subscheme H, the section map on an affine open is the quotient by its defining ideal, followed by the section-ring identification. A section in that ideal has zero class and thus pulls back to zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ι_appLE_apply_topIso_hom: Pullback from V to W along the inclusion is the inverse of the canonical identification on global sections followed by restriction to W. The inverse cancels the identification applied to the global pullback of x along g. What remains is the pullback of x along g restricted to W, as claimed.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ι_appLE_coord: The chart coordinate is the global pullback of the corresponding affine-space coordinate, transported to sections over U. Pulling this section back to W cancels that transport and restricts the global pullback to W.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ι_appLE_self_top_eq_topIso_inv: The preimage of V in its open subscheme is the whole subscheme. The resulting map from sections on V to global sections of that subscheme is the canonical section-ring identification in the indicated direction.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_closure_of_mem_irreducibleComponents: For any point of T and any open neighbourhood of it, irreducibility of T makes that neighbourhood meet V inside T, since V is open and meets T. Thus T is contained in the closure of V. The latter is irreducible. Maximality of the irreducible component T gives equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isOpen_isIrreducible_mem_of_smoot: Choose an affine open containing x. Its section ring is Noetherian by smoothness, and its local ring at x is a domain, since it agrees with the ambient stalk of the smooth scheme. Apply the irreducible-neighbourhood criterion to this affine scheme. The open inclusion carries the resulting neighbourhood to an open irreducible subset of X containing x.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isOpen_isIrreducible_of_iso_spec_:
Let P be the prime corresponding to y. Its local ring is a domain by the stalk hypothesis. The kernel K of the localization at P is therefore prime. If q is a prime contained in P and a lies in K, some element outside P annihilates a by the localization criterion. This element is outside q, so primality of q implies a lies in q. Thus K lies in every prime below P.

The unique minimal prime criterion supplies an irreducible open neighbourhood of P in the spectrum, using Noetherianity. Transport it back along the affine homeomorphism to obtain the required neighbourhood of y.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isOpen_isIrreducible_of_unique_ir: Remove the union of all components that miss z. This is a finite union of closed sets, so its complement is an open neighbourhood of z. Every point of that complement lies in a component, and that component must contain z because it was not removed. The uniqueness hypothesis identifies the component with T₀. Thus the complement is a nonempty open subset of the irreducible space T₀, so it is irreducible.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isOpen_isIrreducible_of_unique_mi: The zero locus of K is irreducible because K is prime, and it contains the point P. If an irreducible component contains P, its defining prime is contained in P and hence contains K by hypothesis. Its closed set is therefore contained in the zero locus of K. Maximality of the component makes the two closed sets equal. There are finitely many components because the ring is Noetherian. The unique component result now provides an irreducible open neighbourhood of P.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_ltSeries_le_of_hasGoingDown: Induct on the length of the prime chain. Lift its last prime to a prime P below Q by going-down, allowing equality of the contractions. For a chain of length zero this prime is the whole lift. Otherwise apply induction to the chain with its last prime removed, using P as the upper bound. The last prime of the lifted shorter chain lies below P. It is strictly smaller because its contraction is the penultimate prime of the original chain, which differs from the contraction of P. Append P to obtain the asserted length and last prime.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_prime_le_under_eq_of_hasGoingDown: If p is the contraction of Q, take Q itself. If p is strictly smaller than that contraction, going-down supplies a prime below Q lying over p.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.finiteType_appTop_of_isAffineOpen_of_smo: The restricted structure map on the affine open V is smooth and thus locally of finite type. Under the affine identification with the spectrum of its global section ring, this is the spectrum map of the indicated scalar map from k. The affine criterion for local finite type makes that ring map of finite type.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClopen_irreducibleComponent_of_smooth: The irreducible component T is closed. For each point in T, choose an open irreducible neighbourhood using smoothness. The closure of that neighbourhood equals T by the component closure result, because they meet at the given point. Thus the neighbourhood lies in T. Every point has such an open neighbourhood inside T, proving that T is also open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isDomain_localization_of_iso_spec: The point y corresponds under the affine identification to a prime of R. The localization of R at this prime identifies with the stalk on its spectrum and hence with the local ring at y. The latter is a domain by hypothesis, so the localization is also a domain.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isDomain_stalk_of_smooth: The local ring at x is regular by the preceding theorem. Every regular local ring is an integral domain.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherianRing_sections_of_isAffineOpe: The global section ring of V is a finite type algebra over k by the preceding result. A field is Noetherian, and a finite type algebra over a Noetherian ring is Noetherian.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isReduced_of_smooth: Every stalk is a domain by smoothness and therefore has no nonzero nilpotent elements. Reducedness can be checked on stalks, proving that X is reduced.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isRegularLocalRing_of_flat_formallyUnram: The dimensions of the two local rings agree by the preceding argument. The maximal ideal of S is the extension of the maximal ideal of R by formal unramifiedness and essential finite type. It needs at most as many generators, which by regularity of R is the common dimension. The height bound in the Noetherian local ring S gives the reverse inequality on the generator count. Equality is the criterion for regularity of S.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isRegularLocalRing_stalk_affineSpace: Affine space is the spectrum of the coordinate polynomial ring over k. A polynomial ring in finitely many variables over a field is regular at each prime. Applying the comparison with the localizations at these primes gives the result for the stalk.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isRegularLocalRing_stalk_of_iso_spec: The isomorphism sends x to a prime of R. The stalk at that point on the spectrum is the localization at that prime. It is regular by hypothesis. The isomorphism identifies it with the stalk at x, which is therefore regular.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isRegularLocalRing_stalk_of_opens: An open inclusion induces an isomorphism on the corresponding local rings. Transport regularity of the local ring of the open subscheme across this isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isRegularLocalRing_stalk_of_smooth: Choose an étale chart around x. The local ring of the affine-space target at the image point is regular. The map on stalks induced by the chart is local, flat, essentially of finite type, and formally unramified, so the local algebra criterion makes the source stalk regular. The chart domain is an open neighbourhood of x, and its local ring at x agrees with the ambient one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isRegularLocalRing_stalk_of_stalkMap_fla: The map on the two stalks is local. The source stalk is Noetherian by its regularity, and the target stalk is Noetherian because the map is essentially of finite type. The local algebra regularity theorem applies using flatness, formal unramifiedness, and essential finite type.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_eq_of_flat_formallyUnramifi: Flatness gives going-down, so the dimension of S is at least that of R. For a formally unramified local map essentially of finite type, the maximal ideal of the target is the extension of the maximal ideal of the source. The preceding generator bound then gives the opposite dimension inequality because R is regular.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_le_of_hasGoingDown: In the base local ring, the last prime of any finite prime chain lies inside the maximal ideal. Under a local ring map this maximal ideal is the contraction of the maximal ideal of S. Going-down lifts the chain to S with the same length, using that maximal ideal as the bound. Every prime chain length in R is therefore bounded by the dimension of S. Taking the supremum gives the inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_le_of_map_maximalIdeal: In the Noetherian local ring S, the height of its maximal ideal is its Krull dimension and is bounded by the minimal number of generators of that ideal. The displayed extension formula bounds this generator count by that of the maximal ideal of R. Regularity of R identifies that count with its dimension, giving the claimed inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_isDomain_stalk: The supplied smoothness gives regularity of the local ring at x, hence that ring is a domain.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_isReduced: Apply the reducedness result for schemes smooth over a field using the given smoothness proof for p.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_isRegularLocalRing_stalk: Apply the regularity result on stalks of a smooth scheme to the supplied smoothness of p and the point x.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.spanFinrank_map_le: Choose a generating set of least size for I. It is finite because R is Noetherian. Its image generates the extended ideal in S and has at most as many elements as the original set. The minimal number of generators of the extension is bounded by this size.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_C_map_C: A constant polynomial belongs to the extended ideal exactly when all its coefficients belong to I. Its only possibly nonzero coefficient is the original scalar, so membership is equivalent to that scalar belonging to I. This identifies the contraction with I.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_comap_symm: Contraction of an ideal twice is contraction along the composite of the two ring maps in the appropriate order. Here the composite applies the isomorphism and then its inverse, so it is the identity on A. The contracted ideal is I.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_symm_comap: The double contraction is along the composite that applies the inverse isomorphism and then the isomorphism. This is the identity on B and returns J.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_fromSpecStalkPoint_eq_of_speciali: The image of the spectrum of the local ring at x consists exactly of the generizations of x. Since y specializes to x, it has a preimage in that spectrum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isClosed_singleton_of_isAffine: Identify the affine scheme with the spectrum of its global section ring. Extend the prime corresponding to a to a maximal ideal. Its point is closed in the spectrum and remains closed under the affine homeomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isClosed_singleton_of_isAffineOpe: A point of U exists by nonemptiness. The open subscheme U is affine, so the result for a nonempty affine scheme gives a closed point of U.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_ltSeries_comap: Contract every prime in the given chain along the ring isomorphism. Contraction preserves inclusion, and it reflects equality because contraction along the inverse isomorphism recovers the original prime. Thus strict inclusions remain strict. The new chain has the same length and its last prime is the contraction of the given last prime.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_ltSeries_of_isMaximal_mvPolynomia:
Induct on the number of variables. For zero variables the maximal ideal itself is a chain of length zero. For the successor step, view the ring as a polynomial ring in one variable over the ring with n variables. The smaller ring is Jacobson because it is of finite type over a field, so the contraction N of the given maximal ideal is maximal. By induction there is a chain of length n ending at N.

Extend the primes in that chain to the one-variable polynomial ring. Extension preserves primality because the quotient by an extended prime is a polynomial ring over a domain. It preserves strict inclusion because contracting along constants recovers the original ideals. The last extended prime is contained in the given maximal ideal and is strictly smaller by the preceding result. Append the maximal ideal and transport the chain back along the polynomial-ring isomorphism.

Reindex the variables by the bijection with the ordinary finite index set. The maximal ideal corresponds to a maximal ideal in the ordinary polynomial ring, where the preceding result gives the chain. Contraction along the isomorphism transports the chain back, preserving its length and recovering the original maximal ideal at its end.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_mem_isClosed_singleton_of_isAffin: Choose a closed point of the affine open subscheme U by the preceding result. It consists of a point of X together with its membership in U. Take those data and the closedness proof in U.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.fromSpecStalkPoint_specializes_iff: The canonical map from the spectrum of the local ring at x into X is a topological embedding. An embedding preserves and reflects specialization, giving the equivalence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaximal_comap_C: Over a Jacobson base the map from S to the quotient by the maximal polynomial ideal is integral. The quotient is a field, so contraction of its zero maximal ideal is maximal in S. That contraction is exactly the contraction of the given polynomial ideal along the constants.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_ringKrullDim_stalk_affineSpace: Under the identification with the polynomial spectrum, the closed point corresponds to a maximal ideal. The polynomial prime-chain result gives a chain of length m ending at that ideal. Transporting this chain to affine space gives distinct points ordered by specialization, all specializing to x. The stalk chain criterion therefore gives dimension at least m.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_ringKrullDim_stalk_of_chain: Each point in the specialization chain is a generization of x, so lift it to the spectrum of the stalk at x. The embedding reflects each specialization as inclusion of the lifted primes. The given points are distinct, so adjacent inclusions of primes are strict. This gives a prime chain of length n in the stalk and hence the lower bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_C_ne_of_isMaximal: If the extension of N were the maximal ideal M′, the polynomial variable would be outside M′, since its coefficient of degree one is 1 outside N. In the field quotient by M′ its class would have an inverse. Thus some polynomial times the variable would agree with 1 modulo the ideal extended from N. Taking constant coefficients forces 1 to lie in N, since the polynomial times the variable has zero constant coefficient. This contradicts that N is proper.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_mvPolynomial_uLift_le: The two index sets are bijective, so renaming the variables gives an isomorphism to the polynomial ring in m variables. Ring isomorphisms preserve Krull dimension, and that polynomial ring over the field has dimension m.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_stalk_eq_of_etale: The étale morphism induces a local map from the stalk on W to the stalk on Y which is flat, formally unramified, and essentially of finite type. Apply the local dimension equality theorem, using regularity of the stalk on W and Noetherianity of the stalk on Y.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_stalk_eq_of_etale_affineSpa: The dimension of the stalk at y is at most m by the affine-space bound. An étale map to affine space over a field takes a closed point to a closed point by the closed-point result. Thus the target stalk at the image of y has dimension at least m by the prime-chain construction. Its dimension equals the source stalk dimension by the étale comparison, giving equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_stalk_le_of_etale: The map on stalks of the étale morphism is local, flat, essentially of finite type, and formally unramified. The source and target rings of this local map satisfy the regularity and Noetherian hypotheses of the dimension equality theorem. Their dimensions are therefore equal, giving the asserted inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_stalk_le_of_etale_affineSpa: The affine-space stalk at the image is regular. The étale stalk dimension comparison bounds the dimension at y by the dimension of that target stalk. The target stalk dimension is bounded by the dimension of the whole affine space via the embedding of its spectrum, and the affine space has dimension m by its polynomial description.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_stalk_le_topologicalKrullDi: The ring dimension of the local ring equals the topological dimension of its spectrum. The canonical map embeds this spectrum into X, and the topological dimension of the embedded subspace is bounded by that of X.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.specializes_of_fromSpecStalk_base_specia: The canonical map from the stalk spectrum is a topological embedding. Apply reflection of specialization to the two image points.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_affineSpace_le_ringK: The affine-space isomorphism identifies it with the spectrum of the coordinate polynomial ring. The topological dimension equals that of this spectrum, which is the ring dimension of the polynomial ring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_le_of_forall_ringKru:
Take any strict chain of irreducible closed subsets of X. Choose the generic point of each subset. Inclusions in the chain give specializations from the larger subsets' generic points to the smaller ones. Distinct closed subsets have distinct generic points.

All these generic points are generizations of the generic point of the smallest subset, so they lift to the spectrum of the local ring there. The embedding reflects specialization, and the distinctness of the image points gives strictness. In reverse order the lifted points form a prime chain of the same length. The local dimension bound therefore bounds the length of the original chain. Taking the supremum over the chains gives the topological bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_spec_le_ringKrullDim: The topological Krull dimension of the prime spectrum of a ring equals the ring's Krull dimension. The displayed inequality follows.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.coordIdeal_eq_comap_coordSubs: The chart ideal for S is defined by pulling back the coordinate subspace ideal for S along the chart's étale map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.HasStrictNormalCrossingsWith.exists_etal: Apply the defining local condition of h at the given point x of the support of Z. This supplies the chart, the assignment for E, and the coordinate set for Z with all the required properties.

At x, choose the local chart, the coordinate set S for Z, and the assignment b for the full list H :: E. Keep the chart and S. Assign b(0) to H and b(i+1) to the i-th entry of E. The old ideal conditions at index 0 give the two possibilities for H. At index i+1 they give the two possibilities for the corresponding tail entry.

If a tail entry uses the coordinate assigned to H, injectivity on the assigned coordinates gives i+1 = 0, which is impossible. If two tail entries use the same coordinate, injectivity gives i+1 = j+1 and hence i = j. The original ideal condition for Z applies to the retained chart and S.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.InStrictNormalCrossingPositionAt.exists_: Unfold the local condition at x. Its witnesses are the neighbourhood, chart, and coordinate assignment, and its three requirements give exactly the desired properties.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordSubspaceIdeal_eq_ofIdealTop_span_co: Take the coordinate functions indexed by S in the coordinate ring of the affine space. The coordinate subspace ideal sheaf is defined by taking the sheaf associated to the ring ideal they generate, giving the displayed formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_iff: Unfold the condition at a point x of the support of Z. It asks for an étale coordinate chart around x and an assignment of optional coordinate indices to the entries of E. An unassigned entry restricts to the unit ideal, and an assigned entry restricts to the corresponding coordinate hyperplane ideal. Distinct assigned entries use distinct coordinates. In the same chart, Z restricts to the ideal of the coordinates indexed by S. These are exactly the witnesses and conditions on the right.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_of_forall_e: For each x in the support of Z, the hypothesis supplies a chart with distinct coordinate indices for the assigned entries of E and the required coordinate ideal for Z. These pointwise data give the defining condition for strict normal crossings along Z.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPositionAt_of_exis: Use the given neighbourhood, chart, and assignment in the definition at x. The three conditions in the hypothesis say that assigned indices are distinct and determine the restrictions of every assigned or unassigned entry of E.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_iff: By definition, the global condition consists of smoothness of each divisor in E and the local chart condition at every point of X. Unfolding it gives exactly the stated conjunction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_iff: The definition imposes two conditions. The ideal D is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor, and the subscheme cut out by D is smooth over the base via its inclusion followed by p. These are the two conditions on the right.
